extracted.intended_audience: data journalists, journalism students, newsroom trainers and editors
extracted.subtask_description: Homepage aggregating handbooks, longform articles, courses and community discussion about data journalism best practices, tools, verification, visualisation, ethics and investigative techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions-oriented storytelling for climate
rubrics_metrics.description: The time is now for journalists to halt the doom and gloom narrative around the climate crisis and instead reframe the narrative with a solutions approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solutions storytelling to engage local communities, highlight practical mitigation efforts and bring local reporters together; the piece cites case studies (Unbias The News and the BBC) as examples of this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualise data — understand provenance and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Data are never neutral ‘givens’, but always situated in a particular context, collected for a particular reason -- and it’s crucial that data journalists understand these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat data as situated: investigate why and how data were collected, what they represent and what they omit; put numbers back into context in reporting so audiences understand limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the unspoken rules of visualisation (and know when to break them)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designers often follow a set of strict conventions when creating visualisations. Kaiser Fung examines the fundamental rules of data visualisation, why they are important, and when it is okay to break them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn standard conventions (e.g., appropriate chart types, scales, labeling) and the reasoning behind them so you can make informed exceptions without misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design data visualisations with empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing data visualisations with empathy: How do you get audience members, much less the journalists presenting a story, to walk a mile in the shoes of a dot? Or a bar chart?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply approaches that foreground the human impact behind data; consider audience perspective, accessibility and how visual choices affect emotional and ethical reception of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of map distortions and choose maps carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to display the three-dimensional world we live in, journalists are forced to distort reality. And every map does so in its own way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand commonly used map projections and their distortions; select mapping methods that minimise misleading impressions and explain trade-offs to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of digital content and UGC
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verification Handbook equips journalists with the knowledge to investigate social media accounts, bots, private messaging apps, information operations, deep fakes, as well as other forms of disinformation and media manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow step-by-step verification processes for user-generated content and digital evidence, especially in emergencies; use the Verification Handbook resources and translations as practical guidance for accuracy and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use OSINT and online search techniques for investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: A Guide To Online Search And Research Techniques For Using UGC And Open Source Information In Investigations — based on the Verification Handbook conclusions — sheds light on the use of open data and open source information to produce critical journalistic investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply systematic online search, geolocation, satellite imagery, metadata analysis and other OSINT techniques; follow the walk-through, step-by-step guidance provided to hone investigation tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and clean data properly (encoding, formats, formulas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses and modules such as Cleaning Data in Excel, File encoding, inspecting & correcting data, Using formatting and basic formulas, Formulas and pivot tables emphasise practical data preparation steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect and correct file encodings, remove extraneous columns, apply spreadsheet formulas and pivot tables, sort and filter appropriately; these foundational cleaning steps are necessary before analysis or visualisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn spreadsheet and data-analysis skills for journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Many resources (Spreadsheets for journalism; Formulas and pivot tables) show journalists how to embrace math with an overview of spreadsheets and functions for beginners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop basic to intermediate spreadsheet skills (functions, joins, pivot tables) so reporters can analyze, summarise and interrogate datasets themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate chart types and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources like Choosing the best graphic forms and Charting Tools for the Newsroom guide journalists on selecting the best graphic forms and tooling for newsroom needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match chart type and tool to the story and data: prioritise clarity, avoid misleading encodings, and consider available newsroom tooling (e.g., Chartbuilder, RAWGraphs, CARTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crediting and labelling of data and graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Crediting and Labelling is listed among modules and discussion topics, emphasising the need to properly credit sources and label visual elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always label axes, scales and data sources clearly; credit datasets and authors; document methodology so readers can verify and contextualise findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and protecting sources in data journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics and Protecting your Sources and articles like Giving data soul: best practices for ethical data journalism highlight ethical considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider harms, privacy and consent when using data; protect vulnerable sources and weigh public interest against risks; apply ethical frameworks throughout the reporting process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know when to hire a data journalist or bring in specialised skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices content includes When to hire a data journalist, helping newsrooms understand staffing and skills decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess projects for technical complexity, data volume, or investigative depth to decide whether to use in-house reporters, hire a data journalist, or contract specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply analytics and predictive techniques responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Modules such as Going Viral Using Social Media Analytics and The power of predictive analytics describe analytical approaches and their applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytics and predictive methods to inform reporting while being mindful of limitations, domain-specific biases and ethical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use open data and multiple datasets (joins and merging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content like Join multiple datasets and A Guide To Online Search encourages combining datasets to enrich stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn safe and correct merging/join techniques, reconcile identifiers and document assumptions when combining datasets to avoid introducing errors.
